summary: Iteration 6 (backend + frontend) for Wallet Top-up 503, Withdrawal lifecycle, Cashback+Milestone, Analytics (wallet/referrals/balances), Settings, and Admin sidebar (8 groups + all sub-items). Backend: 12/12 pytest cases PASSED (test_wallet_iter6.py) — Razorpay 503 graceful; withdrawal hold/approve/complete/reject-with-refund reversal all work; below-min & above-withdrawable rejections work; default sources correctly make admin_credit/cashback non-withdrawable; cashback is idempotent on re-delivered orders; analytics endpoints and balances overview return the required shapes; settings persist. Frontend: exact 8 top-level nav groups render and every sub-item (Catalog=7, Sales&Analytics=10 tab links, Coupons=7 with dialogs for create/bulk, Customer Info=5, Delivery=6, Personal=2) navigates to a working non-blank page. Admin Wallet Management shows liability/withdrawals/balances. Admin Settings shows all cashback/milestone/withdrawal testids and 7 wsrc-* source chips. Customer /wallet shows Add Money dialog with graceful red toast 'Online payment is not configured. Please add Razorpay keys.' and Withdraw dialog opens with amount/method/upi fields. One bug found: withdrawable_balance is under-counted after a rejected withdrawal because the original hold ledger entry (source='withdrawal') is not cleared/negated — so the added refund credit is offset by the still-standing hold in gross-held math. Impact: customer cannot re-withdraw money that was refunded from a rejected withdrawal.

minor.issue: On reject/fail, code inserts a +refund credit entry but leaves the original -withdrawal hold entry as-is. `withdrawable_balance` computes gross-of-allowed-sources minus abs(all withdrawal-source entries), so the refund credit is exactly offset by the still-present hold. Net effect: total balance is correct but withdrawable_balance is 0 for the refunded amount. Fix: on reject/fail, either (a) delete/mark-cancelled the hold ledger entry and exclude cancelled from `held` sum, or (b) set the hold entry source to 'withdrawal_reversed' and skip that source in `held` calc.

ui_bugs.issue: Submit button lacks data-testid="withdraw-submit" (visible label 'Request withdrawal' works via role/name but testid contract from spec is missing).

Status filter chips do not appear to expose data-testid="wm-filter-*" (0 found). Approve button testid also not exposed (only 1 fallback button found via text). Feature works visually but automated status-filter testing lacks selectors.

action_items: Fix withdrawable_balance math for rejected/failed withdrawals so the refunded amount becomes withdrawable again (see backend minor above). Suggested one-liner: on reject/fail, either update the hold ledger row {source:'withdrawal',status:'pending'} to {status:'cancelled'} and change `held` sum to only consider status in ('pending','processing','completed') OR change source to 'withdrawal_reversed'. Then re-verify with test_wallet_iter6.test_withdrawable_and_withdraw_flow (extend it to re-attempt a withdraw after reject).
Add data-testid='withdraw-submit' to Wallet.js Withdraw dialog submit button.
Add data-testid='wm-filter-{status}' chips and 'wm-approve-{id}'/'wm-reject-{id}' action buttons to AdminWalletManagement for cleaner e2e.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/wallet.py withdrawable_balance: current logic double-counts a rejected hold — see action item above.

routers/wallet.py add_wallet_entry recomputes balance_after by full-scan of ledger for every insert (O(n) per write). Under any real concurrency this races and returns incorrect balance_after. Cache balance on user or move to atomic $inc on a user wallet doc.

routers/wallet.py wallet_balance and withdrawable_balance both scan the full ledger for every request; withdrawable_balance calls wallet_balance internally so effectively iterates the ledger twice per call. Cache or aggregate.

routers/wallet.py admin_wallet_balances iterates users sequentially and calls wallet_balance + withdrawable_balance per user (each O(n) scans). For N customers with M ledger entries this is O(N*M). Use a single $group aggregation.

routers/orders.py _grant_rewards: milestone dedup uses (source='milestone', notes=note) — safer to key on (order_id, source='milestone') so re-delivering the same order twice cannot ever double-credit.
routers/wallet.py update_withdrawal: does not clear/negate the original hold entry (see main bug).

routers/settings.py load_settings merges DEFAULTS on top of persisted doc every read but does NOT persist DEFAULTS on first read — so PUT of a partial payload can end up with a stored doc missing several defaults (mostly OK because of merge but confusing).
routers/wallet.py request_withdrawal fetches customer_name via ObjectId(user['id']) — will 500 (not 400) if a non-ObjectId user id sneaks in; wrap try/except and validate.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all 8 groups + every sub-item load; wallet + settings + wallet-mgmt visible; 2 minor missing testids; 1 real math bug on withdrawable after reject)

rca_of_the_issue: Rejection reversal bug: routers/wallet.py update_withdrawal() on status in ('rejected','failed') inserts a positive refund ledger entry but leaves the original hold entry (source='withdrawal', amount=-N) untouched. withdrawable_balance() sums abs(amount) for source='withdrawal' as `held`, and sums positive amounts with source in withdrawable_sources as `gross`. The refund is included in gross AND the hold remains in held ⇒ gross - held includes 0 net gain from the reversal, capping withdrawable at 0 for that amount. Fix by updating the hold entry status to 'cancelled' and excluding non-active/non-completed statuses from `held`, OR change hold source to 'withdrawal_reversed' on reject/fail.
